# Format: <hint><TAB><CASE label><TAB>...   (a hint fires when ANY of its cases fails)
man calloc: "The memory is set to zero." malloc makes no such promise: what does a block malloc hands over hold -- and which bytes of it does your function set?

The subject settles nmemb or size 0 (p.8): "calloc() returns a unique pointer value that can be successfully passed to free()". What does your function hand back then -- and would two such calls hand back the same value?
column5: 0 x 5, 5 x 0 and 0 x 0: three different pointers
column6: 0 x 5, 5 x 0 and 0 x 0: each passed to free()

column1: What does man calloc say calloc() gives when "the multiplication of nmemb and size would result in integer overflow"? And what does nmemb * size give in a size_t when the true product is more than SIZE_MAX -- how can a program tell that it happened?
column4: h x h, h = 2^(half the bits of size_t), so h x h = SIZE_MAX + 1
